Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer are:

From [1] and [2]:

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a 'Party' in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the 'Holder') of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates."

Key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- The definition of Change of Control includes sale/lease/exchange/license/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority ownership.
- Issuance of securities in financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes sale of more than 50% of voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates.

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment of rights under the Agreement in such circumstances requires the other Party's consent if the new controlling party is a competitor.

A lawyer should review:
- The consent requirement for assignment upon Change of Control, especially if the new controller is a competitor.
- The detailed definition of Change of Control and its exceptions.
- Whether the consent right is sufficient protection or if a termination right should be negotiated.
- The implications for both parties in the event of a merger, asset sale, or stock sale.

There is no mention of a notice requirement, only a consent requirement in certain Change of Control scenarios.

Based on the provided context passages, the following parts of the contract related to "Audit Rights" should be reviewed by a lawyer:

This section gives each party the right to audit the books and records of the counterparty to ensure compliance with the contract and the accuracy of reports and payments. There is no mention of the right to audit physical locations in this passage.

A lawyer should review:
- The scope of the audit rights (books and records, but not physical locations).

- The requirement for reasonable written notice.

Summary: Yes, a party has the right to audit the books and records of the counterparty to ensure compliance with the contract, but there is no explicit right to audit physical locations in the provided passage.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer are:

From [1] and [2]:

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a 'Party' in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the 'Holder') of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates."

Key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- The definition of Change of Control includes sale/lease/exchange/license/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority voting control.
- Issuance of securities in financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes sale of more than 50% of voting stock by a holder (other than to an Affiliate).

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment of rights under the Agreement in such circumstances requires the other Party's consent if the new controlling party is a competitor.

A lawyer should review:
- The consent requirement for assignment upon Change of Control, especially if the new controlling party is a competitor.
- The detailed definition of Change of Control and its exceptions.
- Whether the consent requirement could impact business flexibility in M&A or investment scenarios.

answer:
The following parts of the contract relate to "Non-Transferable License" and should be reviewed by a lawyer to assess limitations on the ability of a party to transfer the license to a third party:

From [1] and [5] (INGEVITYCORP_05_16_2016-EX-10.5-INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AGREEMENT):

**Section 3.1 License Grant to Parent:**
- "The foregoing license shall be transferable or sublicensable by Parent Group solely to a Permitted Party, and, subject to the restrictions herein, with any sale or transfer of a Parent business that utilizes the Licensed SpinCo IP. Any such transfer or sublicense shall require the Permitted Party or, in the case of a sale or transfer of a Parent business, the transferee, to agree pursuant to a written agreement to maintain any trade secrets and Information included in the Licensed SpinCo IP in strict confidence. Such agreement shall prohibit any further sublicensing or transfer of rights by the Permitted Party, or, in the case of a sale or transfer of a Parent business, the transferee, or any use of the Licensed SpinCo IP outside the scope of the license granted to Parent herein."

**Section 3.2 License Grant to SpinCo:**
- "Such license shall be transferrable subject to the foregoing restriction with any sale or transfer of a SpinCo business that utilizes such Intellectual Property, but, for the avoidance of doubt, such license shall not otherwise be sublicensable or transferable. Any transfer by SpinCo or a member of its Group shall require the transferee to agree pursuant to a written agreement to maintain any trade secrets and Information included in the transferred Intellectual Property in strict confidence. Such agreement shall prohibit any further transfer of rights by such party or any use of the transferred Intellectual Property outside the scope of the license granted to SpinCo herein."

**Summary of Limitations:**
- The license is generally non-transferable and non-sublicensable except in connection with the sale or transfer of the relevant business (Parent or SpinCo) that utilizes the licensed IP.
- Any permitted transfer requires the transferee to enter into a written agreement to maintain confidentiality and prohibits further transfer or sublicensing.
- Any use of the licensed IP outside the scope of the license is prohibited.

**Conclusion:**  
Yes, the contract limits the ability of a party to transfer the license to a third party, except in specific circumstances (sale or transfer of the business utilizing the IP), and imposes strict conditions on any permitted transfer. These provisions should be carefully reviewed by a lawyer.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer are:

From [1] and [2]:

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a 'Party' in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the 'Holder') of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates."

Summary of key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- Change of Control is defined to include sale/lease/exchange/license/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority voting control.
- Issuance of securities in financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes sale of more than 50% of voting stock by a holder (other than to an Affiliate).

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment of rights under the Agreement in such circumstances requires the other Party’s consent if the new controlling party is a competitor.

A lawyer should review:
- The consent requirement for assignment upon Change of Control, especially if the new controlling party is a competitor.
- The detailed definition of Change of Control and its exceptions.
- The absence of an explicit termination right upon Change of Control.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer are:

From [1] and [2]:

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a 'Party' in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the 'Holder') of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates."

Key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- The definition of Change of Control includes sale/lease/exchange/license/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority voting control.
- Issuance of securities in financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes sale of more than 50% of voting stock by a holder (other than to an Affiliate).

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment of rights under the Agreement in such circumstances requires the other Party's consent if the new controlling party is a competitor.

A lawyer should review:
- The consent requirement for assignment upon Change of Control, especially if the new controlling party is a competitor.
- The detailed definition of Change of Control and its exceptions.
- Whether the consent right is sufficient protection or if a termination right should be negotiated.

Question: Highlight the parts (if any) of this contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer. Details: Does one party have the right to terminate or is consent or notice required of the counterparty if such party undergoes a change of control, such as a merger, stock sale, transfer of all or substantially all of its assets or business, or assignment by operation of law?

Answer:
answer:
Relevant parts of the contract related to "Change Of Control" that should be reviewed by a lawyer are:

From [1] and [2]:

- Section 20.4 Change of Control:  
"Should there be a Change of Control of either Party resulting in the control of such Party by a Third Party which markets or sells a Competing Product in any part of the Territory, then the rights under this Agreement may not be assigned without the express consent of the other Party which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. 'Change of Control' shall mean (a) the sale, lease, exchange, license or disposition of all or substantially all of the Party's assets in one transaction or series of related transactions or (b) a merger or consolidation with an unaffiliated Third Party as a result of which the holders of the Party's issued and outstanding voting securities immediately before such transaction own or control less than a majority of the voting securities of the continuing or surviving entity immediately after such transaction. The issuance by either Party of securities in connection with any financing transaction or public offering shall not be deemed a Change of Control under this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the purposes of Section 6.3(b)(iii): (i) references to a 'Party' in the above definition of Change of Control shall be deemed to include PPI as well as any Affiliate of PPI and (ii) a Change of Control shall also include (in addition to any of the transactions described above in the definition of Change of Control), any sale of securities of PPI or its Affiliates directly by the holder (the 'Holder') of such securities (other than to an Affiliate of such Holder) in which such sale results in a transfer of more than 50% of the outstanding voting stock of PPI or its Affiliates."

Key points for legal review:
- If a Change of Control results in control by a Third Party that markets or sells a Competing Product, assignment of rights under the Agreement requires express consent of the other Party (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
- The definition of Change of Control includes sale/lease/exchange/license/disposition of all or substantially all assets, or a merger/consolidation resulting in a change in majority voting control.
- Issuance of securities in financing or public offering is excluded from Change of Control.
- For certain sections, Change of Control also includes sale of more than 50% of voting stock by a holder (other than to an Affiliate).

There is no explicit right to terminate upon Change of Control, but assignment of rights under the Agreement in such circumstances requires the other Party's consent if the new controlling party is a competitor.

A lawyer should review:
- The consent requirement for assignment upon Change of Control, especially if the new controlling party is a competitor.
- The detailed definition of Change of Control and its exceptions.
- The absence of an explicit termination right upon Change of Control, focusing instead on assignment restrictions and consent requirements.
